**Visual analysis:**

- **Plant part:** Single wheat (or small grain cereal) leaf blade, narrow and elongated
- **Tip:** Brown/necrotic tip — a sign of advanced disease or secondary stress
- **Lesions:** Numerous scattered patches distributed across the entire leaf surface
- **Color/texture:** The lesions appear **grayish-white to tan**, with a distinctly powdery or fluffy surface texture — not discrete sunken spots, but surface-growing colonies
- **Distribution:** Scattered irregularly across the leaf, no strict striped alignment along veins
- **No bright orange/red pustules** ruling out leaf rust or stem rust
- **No yellow striped uredinia** ruling out stripe rust

**Key differentials:**
- **Powdery Mildew:** Grayish-white powdery/fluffy colonies on leaf surface — matches very well
- **Septoria Leaf Blotch:** Tan-brown blotches with dark pycnidia, more angular lesions bounded by veins — less consistent
- **Tan Spot:** Tan lesions with yellow halos, more discrete oval shape — less consistent
- **Stripe Rust:** Yellow-orange pustules in clear stripes — not matching

**Conclusion:** The grayish-white, powdery/fluffy surface colonies scattered across the green leaf are highly characteristic of **Powdery Mildew** (*Blumeria graminis*). This superficial, ectoparasitic fungal growth matches the visual signature well.
